## PM claim + dispatch order — R14, with the ruling made

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), round **R14**, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6089-hook-selftests-derive-counts`.

### Ruling: **option 1** — drop the counts from the step names

The card defers the choice upward on the grounds that this is "a governed-adjacent CI file". ⚠️ That category does not exist: this repo's governed surface is `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. `.github/workflows/**` is ordinary CI surface, so this is a lane-PM call and I am making it.

**Drop the counts from the two step names.** The run's own tail already prints `N passed, N failed` — a number that **cannot lie**, because it is produced by the thing being counted. A step name carrying a hand-copied duplicate with no derivation and no check is the declared≠actual class this lane has spent the day clearing, in the one place a reviewer actually looks.

Option 2 (keep the counts, add the recipe) is rejected: it preserves the duplication and merely documents it, creating a maintenance obligation in a second file when the hook headers already carry that obligation correctly. One authoritative copy beats two synchronised ones.

**The cost note (line 48) keeps its numbers**, restated as a **dated measurement** — e.g. "measured on `origin/main` @ `<sha>`". A timing note is history and is honest as history; a step label is a live claim. Make that distinction visible in the file so the next editor knows why one kept its number and the other did not.

### ⚠️ Disclosure: this workflow is this seat's own

`hook-selftests.yml` landed via **PR #6022 (card #5754)**, accepted by this seat today. The defect is ours, filed by a dev on a later card. Say so plainly in the PR body — the record should show the lane caught its own hazard rather than implying an inherited one.

### Timing — this is the reason it goes now

Two draft PRs against the hooks each grow a matrix and **neither touches this workflow** (both are correctly port-scoped): **#6087** takes `guard-shared-stash` 32 → 41, **#6046** takes `guard-main-checkout-bash` 100 → 121. Landing this first makes both merges non-events instead of two moments where a step name silently becomes wrong.

⚠️ So do **not** update the counts to 41/121 — that would just re-arm the same drift one cycle later. Remove them.

### Verification

Be honest about what can be verified here: a step **name** has no runtime behaviour, so there is no assertion to add and no gate that would have caught this.

- Confirm the workflow still parses and its job/step structure is unchanged — `yaml.safe_load` and a before/after of the step ids, not just the names.
- ⚠️ Check whether any test pins these step names before you change them. `scripts/__tests__/` contains workflow-pinning tests (`ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` and siblings) that assert on workflow content; if one names these steps, it is part of your diff. **Verify rather than assume** — a stale line number or an assumed absence has cost this lane a round twice today.
- Run the two self-tests themselves so the PR records what the tails currently print, demonstrating the number the labels were duplicating is already available.
- Gates per your diff, each quoting its own verdict line.

⛔ Out of scope: the hooks, their self-tests, the matrices, and PRs #6087 / #6046. ⛔ Do not "fix" the drift by changing what the workflow runs.

⛔ Never `git stash` — shared stack, other agents are using it now.

⚠️ Lead your report comment with the **literal text** `os-dev-report` on the first line, never an HTML comment — GitHub's sanitizer strips HTML-comment markers.

Refs: #6042 / PR #6087 · #5789 / PR #6046 · #5754 / PR #6022 · #3721.
